questions.q: What must be running in the cluster before an HPA can scale based on CPU utilization?
options: A StorageClass with dynamic provisioning
metrics-server, which aggregates real-time resource usage per Pod for the HPA controller to read
An Ingress Controller
The cluster autoscaler
questions.explain: metrics-server is the cluster add-on that collects CPU/memory usage data. Without it, an HPA based on resource utilization has no metric data to act on.

questions.q: Why does a resource request matter for an HPA target like averageUtilization: 70 on CPU?
options: Utilization percentage is measured against the Pod's requested CPU, so without a request value, 'utilization' has nothing to be a percentage of
Requests are unrelated to HPA behavior
Requests determine which namespace the HPA operates in
The request value sets the maxReplicas automatically
questions.explain: averageUtilization expresses actual usage as a percentage of the container's requested CPU. Without a CPU request set, there's no baseline to compute that percentage against.

questions.q: What field on a HorizontalPodAutoscaler specifies which Deployment it scales?
options: metadata.name
spec.metrics
spec.scaleTargetRef
spec.selector
questions.explain: scaleTargetRef identifies the target resource (typically a Deployment) whose replica count the HPA will adjust.

questions.q: Northbridge sets minReplicas: 3 and maxReplicas: 30 on the checkout HPA. What does maxReplicas protect against?
options: Pods being scheduled onto the wrong node
Checkout ever dropping below 3 replicas during low traffic
The HPA controller crashing under load
Unbounded scaling — protecting the cluster's capacity and cloud costs if a metric spikes unexpectedly or a bug causes runaway resource usage
questions.explain: maxReplicas is a ceiling that prevents the HPA from scaling without bound, protecting against runaway costs or cluster exhaustion from a metric spike or a misbehaving app.

questions.q: Can an HPA scale based on something other than built-in CPU/memory resource metrics?
options: Yes — it can also use memory utilization, or custom/external metrics like queue depth, via Pods or External metric types with an appropriate metrics adapter
Yes, but only by replacing metrics-server entirely
No, custom metrics require a completely separate autoscaler object
No, HPA only ever supports CPU utilization
questions.explain: Beyond CPU, an HPA can target memory utilization the same way, or use Pods/External metric types to scale on custom or external metrics such as a message queue's depth, given an appropriate metrics adapter.
